mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining (1-month change < 0), or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% in a 3-month window, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (1-month change < 0), or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and rising), the increased cost of capital reduces corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and rising, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases (1-month change > 0), or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 104.0 in a 1-month window, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 104.0, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (defined by quarterly GDP above $16,800 billion and unemployment below 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the market prices in the end of the cycle, leading to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 > 16800 and UNRATE < 4.0, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month indicates a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines (1-month change < 0), or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
